Clock Trace Topology: Star to Daisy Chain

The file /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb has a 100 MHz clock (net CLK) routed as a star topology: one source (U1) fans out to three loads (U2, U3, U4) through a common hub. A series-termination resistor footprint (R_TERM, 22R) sits in a scratch area with no net connection.

Re-route CLK as a daisy chain with R_TERM inserted as a series terminator between the source and the first load. Split the net into CLK_PRE (source side) and CLK (load side). Move R_TERM to a position between U1 and the load chain.

Requirements:
1. Net CLK_PRE exists; U1 output pad is on CLK_PRE.
2. Net CLK exists; U2, U3, U4 input pads are on CLK.
3. R_TERM pad "1" is on CLK_PRE; R_TERM pad "2" is on CLK.
4. CLK net topology is a chain (no node with 3+ segments meeting - no star junction).
5. Total CLK segment length <= 100 mm.

Write /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb.
source: Howard Johnson, *High-Speed Digital Design* Johnson ch. 5, TI / Analog Devices / Nordic / Microchip PCB layout app notes (Microchip clock layout)
